description.content: Renders tabular data with virtualization along the vertical and horizontal axes. Row heights and column widths must be known ahead of time and specified as properties.
Scrolling is done through the imperative handle (ref): see scrollToCell and scrollToPosition.

description.content: Responsible for rendering a group of cells given their index ranges.

This is an advanced property. It is useful for situations where the Grid requires additional, overlayed UI (such as a Gantt chart or a calendar application). The easiest way to override it is to decorate defaultCellRangeRenderer.
Defaults to defaultCellRangeRenderer.
Responsible for rendering a cell given an row and column index. It receives columnIndex, isScrolling, isVisible, key, parent, rowIndex, and style parameters.
The style parameter specifies how the cell is to be sized and positioned and must be passed through to the rendered cell element. The key parameter must also be applied to the rendered element.
Optional custom CSS class name to attach to root Grid element.
Number of columns in grid.

Either a fixed column width (number) or a function that returns the width of a column given its index: ({ index: number }): number. If function is used, specify estimatedColumnSize for more consistent scrolling behavior.

description.content: Height of Grid; this property determines the number of visible (vs virtualized) rows. Required, unless a scrollElement is specified.
With a scrollElement, the height of the scroll element's viewport is used instead; this prop is then only used until the scroll element has been measured (e.g. during server rendering).
Optional custom id to attach to root Grid element.

Horizontal scroll offset to initially render (and scroll to) the Grid at. Only the initial value is used: changing this prop later has no effect (use scrollToPosition to scroll). This also works with server rendering: the cells at this offset are rendered on the server, and they stay in place when the page is hydrated.

Vertical scroll offset to initially render (and scroll to) the Grid at. Only the initial value is used: changing this prop later has no effect (use scrollToPosition to scroll). This also works with server rendering: the cells at this offset are rendered on the server, and they stay in place when the page is hydrated. Ignored if a scrollElement is specified (which then determines the vertical offset).

Prevents re-rendering of visible cells on scroll end. (Opts out of the isScrolling param passed to cellRangeRenderer, to avoid the extra render when scroll stops.) Visible cells are still re-rendered when the Grid's props change or forceUpdate() is called.

description.content: Number of columns to render before/after the visible slice of the grid. This can help reduce flickering during scrolling on certain browsers/devices.

Note that this property has performance implications: the higher the value, the more work needs to be done in reaction to each scroll event. Aim to use the lowest value possible that still generally avoids any empty space from appearing during normal scrolling.

overscanColumnCount.name: overscanColumnCount

description.content: Responsible for calculating the number of cells to overscan before and after a specified range. By default, cells are overscanned in the direction the user is scrolling. This function receives direction, cellCount, scrollDirection, overscanCellsCount, startIndex, and stopIndex parameters and returns an { overscanStartIndex, overscanStopIndex } object.
Defaults to defaultOverscanIndicesGetter.
Number of rows to render above/below the visible slice of the grid. This can help reduce flickering during scrolling on certain browsers/devices.

Note that this property has performance implications: the higher the value, the more work needs to be done in reaction to each scroll event. The default value (10) is a good starting point; lower it if possible.

description.content: Number of rows in grid.

Either a fixed row height (number) or a function that returns the height of a row given its index: ({ index: number }): number. If function is used, specify estimatedRowSize for more consistent scrolling behavior.
Element that scrolls the Grid (instead of the Grid scrolling itself): "window", or a scrollable DOM element (e.g. a container that the Grid is rendered within, along with other content).

The Grid then renders at its full height (it may still scroll horizontally itself), renders only the rows visible within the scroll element's viewport, and its scroll methods scroll the scroll element. Its position within the scroll element is measured when the scroll element scrolls or is resized, and when the Grid re-renders (e.g. call forceUpdate() if content above the Grid changes size without the Grid re-rendering). Pass null while the scroll element isn't available yet (e.g. before a ref to it has been attached); the Grid then renders the rows at its top.
